title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LC0RB_0LE0LD_1LC---_0RA1LF_1LA1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LC0RB_0LE0LD_1LC---_0RA1LF_1LA1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the four passes over the regular parts of the tape and the halting situation (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape back and forth. Seen at the left end, the tape is 0 0 1, a left part made of blocks a = 0011 separated by short pieces (b, 0 13, 0 12, 0 1 0 12), then a long run bn of the word b = 010111, then the fixed end 0 14 b2 0 1. The run bn gets one more copy on most round trips, so the tape grows like the square root of the step count; the left part is rewritten like the low digits of a counter.
Where a halt would come from. Only D reading a 1 halts, and D is entered only from C reading a 1; so 1 C>1 halts (halt_C). In the run C reads a 1 only with a 0 to its left.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 54,112 cells have been visited and 24,090 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).

claims.title: Every way to a halt
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the machine is in 1 1 A>1, 1 1 B>0 or 1 1 D>0; no other configuration halts within three steps.

claims.title: Four passes
claims.text: B moving right turns 0 0 (011101)n into (010001)n 0 0 and 0 0 (1001)n into (1010)n 0 0; moving left, C turns (000101)n 0 into 0 (101110)n and E turns (1010)n 1 into 1 (0011)n. All for any n.

claims.title: The halting situation
claims.text: 1 C>1 halts after two steps; D is entered only from C reading a 1.

claims.title: Never close to halting
claims.text: In the first 106 steps C reads a 1 36,496 times, always as 100[1]111, with a 0 to its left.

claims.title: The shape at the left end
claims.text: At the left-end turns of the first 3·106 steps the tape is 0 0 1, a part made of a-blocks and short separators, bn, and 0 14 b2 0 1. In the first 106 steps n grows by 1 on 198 round trips, by 2 on 23 and by 0 on 6.

claims.title: The left part at 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: At step 1,982,205,406 the left-end turn reads C> (01)4 (1100)20 1 1 0 1 0 13 (0011)111 0 1 (0110)21 13 (0011)71 0 13 (0011)4 (010111)12563 0 14 …. The left part is a few runs of the word 0011 (in its rotations) with counts in the hundreds. Window-based closed tape languages with windows of 3 to 7 cells find no closed set.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The next step is the rule by which a round trip rewrites the left part, and when it hands a copy of b to the right part.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine sweeps a tape whose right part is one six-cell word repeated and whose left part changes like a counter. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 54,112 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A counter in front of a crystal
html: Stop the simulator each time the head turns at the left end, and write a for 0011 and b for 010111:

445,663  0 0 1 b a13 0 13 a7 0 12 0 13 b161 0 14 b2 0 1
  495,569  0 0 1 a5 0 13 a13 0 1 0 12 a2 0 13 a2 b170 0 14 b2 0 1
2,965,211  0 0 1 a22 0 13 a18 0 12 0 13 b442 0 14 b2 0 1

The long run of b is the bulk of the tape. It gets one more copy on most round trips (198 of the first 227), so the tape grows like the square root of the step count. In front of it is a short left part of a-blocks and separators, which is rewritten on each trip like the low digits of a counter.

Each pass is a fast rewrite of one word at a time. Moving right, B turns every 011101 into 010001 (14 steps a word) and every 1001 into 1010; moving left, C turns every 000101 into 101110 and E turns every 1010 back into 0011. For example 0 0 B>011101 011101 becomes 010001 010001 0 0 B> after 28 steps. Lean proves all four rules for every n.

The only halt is 1 C>1 (halt_C): C writes a 0 and steps left onto a 1 in state D, which has no transition for 1. In the run C reads a 1 only as 100[1]111. The open step is the exact rule of the left part and why it never puts a 1 to the left of C there.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).
After 109 steps the tape spans 54,112 cells (26,018 left of the start, 13,535 right), with a density of 1s of 0.445.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: two-sided bouncer with a counter-like left part and a period-6 right part
summary: Full sweeps over a tape with two regular parts: on the left, blocks of 0011 with separators that change like a counter; on the right, the six-cell word 010111 repeated, one more copy on most round trips. Open.
